backlog.title: Stabilization: fix 6 adversarial-probe findings (BUG-001..BUG-006)
backlog.description: Fix one critical dictionary-calibration defect (common English words pop menus), three major contract/behavior bugs (stale-prefix Tab corruption, multi-segment secret leakage, disable-on-bad-dictionary violated during restore), one major feature-reachability flaw (chained completion unreachable after session restore), and one minor cadence bug (phrase demotion sweep skipped during restore replay). All fixes ride on the existing 523-test suite; each subtask implies failing-test-first TDD; a consolidated adversarial regression suite and changeset-level docs sweep close the phase.

milestones.title: Dictionary recalibration (BUG-001, Critical)
milestones.description: Replace the length-sorted provisional artifact with a real frequency-ranked dictionary and recalibrate the admission bands so ordinary English prose never triggers menus, restoring PRD §04/§07 admission semantics.

tasks.title: Real frequency corpus + artifact regeneration

subtasks.title: Vendor FrequencyWords en_50k corpus as build input
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_88fc3a66fd74/bugfix/001_9e0f97150b68/architecture/external_deps.md §1 and system_context.md BUG-001. Today's dict was built by tools/gen-provisional-tsv.mjs from a LENGTH-sorted system word list (rank ordering unrelated to frequency). tools/build-dict.mjs already consumes `word<TAB>count` TSVs (mergeTsv sums counts across files/dup keys; KEY_RE=/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,31}$/ filter; count-DESC sort; slice(0, DICT_N=70_000)). .gitignore does not cover tools/ or *.tsv, so the corpus is committable. No runtime deps may be added.
2. INPUT: Raw corpus from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hermitdave/FrequencyWords/master/content/2018/en/en_50k.txt (verified reachable via curl; ~600KB, `word count` SPACE-separated per line, line order = rank). Fallback if license/sanity fails: Norvig count_1w.txt (already TAB-separated, slice to top ~60k).
3. LOGIC: Download once, convert to TAB-separated TSV, commit at tools/corpus/en-50k.tsv (plus a short tools/corpus/README.md or header comment recording source URL, license, retrieval date/command, and the conversion). Run sanity assertions: file head contains the/you/i/to/a; the/with/this all appear in the top 100 lines; all lines match KEY_RE or are documented as filtered at build. Do NOT change build-dict.mjs behavior in this subtask — the existing merge/filter/sort/quant pipeline consumes the TSV as-is. Prefer the RAW (non-lemmatized) list: lemmatized variants would miss inflected common forms which would then fall to rank-group-0 'rare'.
4. OUTPUT: Committed tools/corpus/en-50k.tsv consumable by `node tools/build-dict.mjs --out <path> tools/corpus/en-50k.tsv` for consumption by P1.M1.T1.S2; provenance documented.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] tools/corpus provenance note (source URL, license, retrieval command) ships WITH this subtask. README §Dictionary build sync rides with P1.M1.T1.S2 and the final changeset sweep.

tasks.title: Admission-band recalibration + shipped-dict calibration gates
tasks.description: Recalibrate the §04 admission bands in src/core/score.ts against the real-corpus rank distribution so the top ~1,000 English words reject, and add calibration tests that pin the artifact so this class of drift can never ship silently again.

subtasks.title: Recalibrate REJECT/MID band constants against real-corpus ranks
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/external_deps.md §2 and system_context.md BUG-001. With the current quant curve (denominator fixed at DICT_N=70,000 regardless of kept count): rank 100→q150, rank 500→q114, rank 1000→q98, rank 5000→q64, rank 20000→q30. PRD requires q>=REJECT to cover 'the/with/this/them/context'-class words (today REJECT=220 only covers ranks 0-3). Bands live at src/core/score.ts REJECT_COMMON_THRESHOLD (~L49) and MID_FREQ_THRESHOLD (~L54) and are the sanctioned 'only tuning surface' (spec/04, spec/08) — baked constants, never config/env.
2. INPUT: Regenerated dict/common-en.bin from P1.M1.T1.S2 (real rank ordering, format v1 unchanged).
3. LOGIC: Retune the two constants so that measured against the regenerated artifact: the top ~1,000 corpus ranks are rejected (starting point REJECT≈100, per external_deps.md arithmetic), the next few thousand ranks land group 2 (starting point MID≈40), and the tail stays group 1. Pin exact values via a small measurement (node -e lookups over the vendored TSV ranks), not guesses. Update the JSDoc band table on both constants and the module header in score.ts. Adjust affected unit tests (test/score.test.ts band-table cases) to the new constants. Do NOT change quant(), DICT_N, the binary format, or DICT_VERSION — the curve-change alternative requires a format-version bump per spec/03 L102-103 and is out of scope unless band widening demonstrably fails calibration review.
4. OUTPUT: New REJECT_COMMON_THRESHOLD/MID_FREQ_THRESHOLD values in src/core/score.ts such that admit() rejects lookup('the')/lookup('with')/lookup('this')/lookup('them') and lands 'context'-class words rejected-or-group-2, consumed by P1.M1.T2.S2's calibration test.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on both constants + score.ts header band table updated with the recalibrated rationale. No user-facing/config surface change.

milestones.title: Secret-leak hardening (BUG-003)
milestones.description: Close the multi-segment secret leakage: structural key shapes are masked out of raw text before tokenization, and token-level entropy rules catch residue fragments, so realistic API keys never become candidates.

tasks.title: Raw-text secret masking pass (pre-segmentation)
tasks.description: Add a masking function over raw segment text that neutralizes structured key windows (AWS, Slack, JWT, OpenAI, GitHub, Google shapes) before tokenize() can fragment them, wired into the write path in src/pi/ingest.ts.

subtasks.title: maskSecrets() window scan wired into #admitSegment
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/external_deps.md §3 and system_context.md BUG-003. Root cause: prefix rules (src/core/shapeGate.ts SECRET_PREFIXES ~L78) never match after src/core/segment.ts tokenize splits keys at '/','-','.'; base64 rule requires '+/' which base64url never contains; digit+symbol ratio rarely >0.4 for mixed-case payloads. Gating is WRITE-time only (passesShape at ingest.ts:314; read path trusts the store), so any gate gap is a direct leak. Raw un-tokenized segment strings are available in IngestPipeline.#admitSegment (~ingest.ts:330) — the natural masking seam.
2. INPUT: Raw segment string (newline-free) inside #admitSegment before tokenize(segment).
3. LOGIC: Add exported maskSecrets(segment: string): string to src/core/shapeGate.ts (secret rules stay always-on, non-configurable) that replaces matched windows with an inert placeholder (e.g. spaces) so tokenize() never emits key bytes. Regex inventory (gitleaks-derived; validate each against the PRD's probe keys before landing): AWS 40-char run `[0-9a-zA-Z/+]{40}` (context-optional bare run); AKIA-class IDs `(A3T[A-Z0-9]|AKIA|AGPA|AIDA|AROA|AIPA|ANPA|ANVA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}`; Slack `xox[baprs]-[0-9]{10,13}-[0-9]{10,13}[a-zA-Z0-9]*`; JWT `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*` (also gitleaks' stricter ey..ey.. variant); OpenAI legacy `sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20}T3BlbkFJ[a-zA-Z0-9]{20}` and modern `sk-(proj-|svcacct-|admin-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}`; GitHub `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`, `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,}`; Google `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}`. Wire `segment = maskSecrets(segment)` at the top of #admitSegment. Unit tests: each realistic PRD format (AWS wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY, xoxb tail, JWT with dots, sk-proj-4t7RX2bQ9wLm3vN8xKpZ6dJh1cA5eFgH0iU) fully masked → zero CandidateDrafts from the masked span; false-positive guards: normal prose, URLs, zendesk/lwlock fixture vocabulary must pass through unmasked. Mock nothing — pure function over strings.
4. OUTPUT: maskSecrets() export in src/core/shapeGate.ts + the ingest seam, for consumption by P1.M2.T2.S1 (token rules layer under it) and P1.M5.T1.S2 e2e probes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on maskSecrets enumerating the rule inventory and its always-on status. README security posture rides with the final changeset sweep.

tasks.title: Token-level high-entropy secret rules
tasks.description: Extend isSecretShaped with base64url-run and charset-relative entropy rules so residue fragments that survive masking (standalone high-entropy tokens with no structural prefix) are still rejected.

subtasks.title: base64url run + charset-relative entropy rules in isSecretShaped
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/external_deps.md §3. isSecretShaped (src/core/shapeGate.ts:143-191, private; sole call site passesShape L110) currently requires '+/' for base64 runs (MIN_BASE64_RUN=24) — base64url payloads (no punct) never fire. Entropy must be charset-relative: random base64 ≈6 bits/char max, hex = 4.0, English prose ≈4.0-4.2 — a flat >=3.5 threshold false-positives on ordinary words.
2. INPUT: CandidateDraft.display string at the existing passesShape call path; maskSecrets() from P1.M2.T1.S1 already removed structured keys upstream, so these rules target standalone residue tokens.
3. LOGIC: In isSecretShaped add: (a) base64url run rule — length >=16 matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}` with >=1 lowercase, >=1 uppercase, AND >=2 digits, WITHOUT any '+/' requirement; (b) optional Shannon-entropy refinement — flag base64-charset runs iff entropy >= 4.5 bits/char AND contains a digit AND (mixed case or symbol); hex runs iff entropy >= 3.0. Keep rules baked/non-configurable per spec/04. False-positive corpus guard: camelCase identifiers (fixRoundingError, HTTPServer), SCREAMING_CASE constants, hexish 13-19 band admissions, and fixture vocabulary (zendesk, lwlock, nrel, f3a9c2e) MUST still pass the gate — pin each in tests. Run the unit suite against the PRD repro: standalone 'wJalrXUtnFEMI' (13 chars, mixed case, no digits — expected outcome: NOT caught by (a); caught upstream only by masking; document this boundary in the rule's JSDoc) and 'bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY' (19 chars mixed case — caught if digits present, else masking is the catcher; pin actual behavior).
4. OUTPUT: Hardened isSecretShaped rules layered under maskSecrets, consumed by P1.M5.T1.S2 e2e probes with realistic keys.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the new rules documenting thresholds and the masking/entropy layering. No config surface change.

milestones.title: Restore-path contracts (BUG-004, BUG-006)
milestones.description: Honor the disable-on-bad-dictionary contract during session restore replay and run the 40-ordinal phrase demotion sweep at restore completion.

tasks.title: Honor disable-on-bad-dictionary during restore replay
tasks.description: Expose sticky dictionary-load failure, gate ingestion on it per segment, and abort the restoreFromHistory replay loop so a bad table never ingests history as rank-group-0 candidates.

subtasks.title: Expose lazy-dictionary failure state + per-segment disable gate in IngestPipeline
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-004. createLazyDictionary (src/pi/index.ts ~L79-130) has sticky failure (onLoadError fired exactly once, later lookups null) but exposes NO failure state — no getter, no throw. The `disabled` flag is set in onLoadError but checked only in session_start/message_end; at session_start the lazy dict hasn't loaded yet, so restore always starts. Lookup never throws (Dictionary contract), so gating must come from an explicit failure probe.
2. INPUT: None from other subtasks — this is the enabling seam.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add a failure probe to the lazy dictionary object (e.g. `get failed(): boolean`, or an optional field on the Dictionary shape in src/core/types.ts kept backward-compatible) — true once the load threw, never resets. (b) Add an optional constructor option `isDisabled?: () => boolean` to IngestPipeline (src/pi/ingest.ts), checked at the TOP of processText AND per segment inside #admitSegment's admission loop, so failure observed mid-message stops admissions within that message (otherwise every lookup in message 1 returns null → all its words admitted as group 0 — exactly the bug). Wire it in src/pi/index.ts factory: `isDisabled: () => disabled` (closure already holds `disabled`). Mock nothing — unit-test with a real createLazyDictionary on a nonexistent path.
4. OUTPUT: Observable failure state + per-segment gate, consumed by P1.M3.T1.S2's restore abort and testable directly (processText with a failed dict stores nothing).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the new probe/option. No user-facing/config surface change (option is internal wiring, not config).

subtasks.title: Abort restoreFromHistory replay on dictionary failure
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-004. restoreFromHistory (src/pi/ingest.ts ~L426-443) is a fire-and-forget `void (async () => {...})()` loop: per entry `await pipeline.processText(text, fromUser)` inside try/catch-continue — no abort check. It takes `pipeline: Pick<IngestPipeline, 'processText'>`. Existing notify-once behavior (ctx.ui.notify('hapax: dictionary failed to load', 'error') + disabled=true in onLoadError) must be preserved. Test helpers: test/ingest-restore.test.ts fakeSm(opts)/fakePipeline()/settle()=vi.waitFor.
2. INPUT: The isDisabled predicate + lazy-dict failure probe from P1.M3.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Extend restoreFromHistory to abort the replay when the dictionary has failed — check at the top of the per-entry loop (and rely on the per-segment gate from P1.M3.T1.S1 to stop the in-flight message). Signature change: accept the abort capability via an optional predicate parameter (e.g. `shouldAbort?: () => boolean`) or widen the Pick to include the new gate — choose the minimal-signature option consistent with the existing Pick style; wire it in src/pi/index.ts session_start. Mock: use a real IngestPipeline with createLazyDictionary('/nonexistent') and the fakeSm helper with prose messages.
4. OUTPUT: restoreFromHistory that, given a bad dict path, replays ZERO candidates: after settle(), store.size === 0 and rankMatches(store, 'with') === [] (strictly pin zero — the per-segment gate must prevent even the triggering message's words). Notify still fires exactly once. Consumed by P1.M5.T1.S2 probes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on restoreFromHistory documenting the abort contract. README restore/disable behavior rides with the final changeset sweep.

tasks.title: Phrase demotion sweep after restore replay
tasks.description: Run sweepPhraseDemotions once when the restore replay completes so stale fast-path phrases from ancient history do not survive resume as completion candidates.

subtasks.title: Public sweepPhrases() on IngestPipeline called at restore tail
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-006. The sweep fires ONLY in #drainQueue's finally block (src/pi/ingest.ts ~L249: `this.#onSweepPhrases?.()`, wired in index.ts to `sessionStore.sweepPhraseDemotions()` behind config.enablePhrases). restoreFromHistory calls processText directly, bypassing the queue, so no sweep runs during/after replay. store.sweepPhraseDemotions() (src/core/store.ts:825) demotes non-sticky fast-path phrases with count<2 when now - firstSeenOrdinal >= 40.
2. INPUT: The abort-aware restoreFromHistory from P1.M3.T1.S2 (same file; call-site insertion point is the async IIFE's tail after the entry loop, and it must be SKIPPED when the replay aborted — an aborted replay with a bad dict must not sweep a store it never populated).
3. LOGIC: Add a public `sweepPhrases(): void` method on IngestPipeline that invokes the existing #onSweepPhrases hook (same try/catch-never-wedge pattern as #drainQueue). Call it once after the restore replay loop completes normally. Mock: reuse the ingest-restore test helpers; PRD repro as the test — onMessageEnd a fast-path all-rare phrase ('zorblat quuxified mumblewords') + flush yields candidates, then 45 direct processText('filler') restore-style calls followed by the restore-tail sweep must demote them (mirror of the live-path demotion test in test/ingest-pipeline.test.ts ~L409-460).
4. OUTPUT: Demotion cadence honored after resume; consumed by P1.M5.T1.S2 probes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on sweepPhrases() and the restore-tail call. No user-facing/config surface change.

milestones.title: Completion-UI safety & chain reachability (BUG-002, BUG-005)
milestones.description: Make the display provider incapable of returning a stale prefix (Tab can never corrupt typed text), and restore chained-completion reachability after phrases have been learned or a session restored.

tasks.title: Never re-serve a stale prefix from the display provider
tasks.description: Add a prefix-change-invalidates-the-anchor exception mirroring the existing completionSincePaint fix, so pi-tui's applyCompletion can never replace the wrong span during a suppression window.

subtasks.title: Prefix-anchor invalidation in createDisplayProvider + faithful editor-sim regression
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-002 and external_deps.md §4. Rule 4d (src/pi/provider.ts:674-682) returns copyOf(displayedItems) with the STALE displayedPrefix while the buffer holds more characters. pi-tui stores suggestions.prefix from every rendered response (editor.js:1925-26) and Tab (editor.js:540-551; also single-item force-apply 1903-1912) calls applyCompletion which deletes exactly prefix.length chars before the cursor verbatim (autocomplete.js:265-267: slice(0, cursorCol - prefix.length)) with NO re-verification at Tab time. The 4c-exception (completionSincePaint, provider.ts:659-673, flag at 556/590, set in applyCompletion wrapper 690) is the established pattern for exactly this hazard class. isHapax classification (step 2-3, provider.ts:634-642) already guarantees result.prefix === live.prefix computed from the CURRENT buffer, so any freshly painted result is anchor-safe.
2. INPUT: None from other subtasks — self-contained within createDisplayProvider (provider.ts:626-695).
3. LOGIC: Insert a new exception branch BEFORE rule 4d (mirroring 4c's structure and comment style): if result.prefix !== displayedPrefix, paint(items, result.prefix) immediately and return the fresh set — suppression may only re-serve a displayed set whose prefix still suffix-matches the current buffer. Identical-prefix narrowing (set changes, prefix unchanged) keeps the existing suppression behavior (no flicker regression). State the hard invariant in a comment: the provider never returns a prefix that is not the exact suffix of the current line at the cursor. Build a NEW faithful applyCompletion test helper (existing provider-display.test.ts mocks do NOT model deletion): mirror autocomplete.js slice semantics — `before = line.slice(0, col - prefix.length); after = line.slice(col); return before + item.value + after`. Regression test = the PRD repro: store with zendesk+zephyr; type 'z' (delegate), 'e' → paints {zendesk,zephyr}@'ze'; type 'p' within 100ms (fake timers per existing harness) → provider must NOT return prefix 'ze'; Tab-apply must yield 'zephyr'-family text, never 'zzendesk'. Also cover Tab after a pause (no new keystroke) following the suppressed one. Mock: base provider mock as in test/provider-display.test.ts:78-90 but extended with the faithful deletion math.
4. OUTPUT: createDisplayProvider incapable of returning a stale prefix; the editor-sim helper exported from the test for reuse by P1.M5.T1.S1 probes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Comment block on the new exception mirroring the 4c-exception's documentation (why stale anchors destroy text). No user-facing/config/API surface change.

tasks.title: Restore chained-completion reachability after phrase learning
tasks.description: Exempt successor-bearing bare words from constituent suppression and arm the chain on phrase acceptance, so the M2 zero-typing chain works in resumed sessions where phrases already exist.

subtasks.title: Successor-aware constituent-suppression exemption in rankMatches
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-005. phraseSalience (src/core/query.ts:112: 1.2·Σ constituents + 2.0·log2(1+count) when count>=2, PHRASE_MULTIPLIER=1.2 at L83) mathematically always exceeds the first word's own salience, and phraseSuppresses (L133: phraseSal >= wordSal, tie→phrase) therefore ALWAYS removes the bare word from every menu once a phrase starting with it exists (suppression loop query.ts ~L222-232). Store API store.topSuccessors(word) (store.ts:856, O(1), frozen NO_SUCCESSORS on miss) is the ready-made has-successors predicate. CRITICAL: test/acceptance.test.ts:606-610 currently PINS the bug (`expect(menu.map(m=>m.description)).toEqual(['phrase','phrase'])` after nrel.jsonl replay) and the fixture-phase comment at L498-514 works around it — both must be updated to the fixed behavior, and test/chain.test.ts L17-22 documents the same 'seeding order gotcha'.
2. INPUT: None from other subtasks — self-contained in src/core/query.ts rankMatches.
3. LOGIC: In the constituent-suppression loop, skip removing the bare first word when store.topSuccessors(firstWord).length > 0 (the word can arm the chain, so it must stay acceptable; it co-presents BELOW the phrase since salience sorts it after). Words without successors keep today's suppression (spec §06 behavior preserved where it is harmless). With enablePhrases=false the successor index is empty → behavior identical to today. Unit tests: full NREL-style replay (or test/fixtures/sessions/nrel.jsonl) then rankMatches(store,'natio') MUST contain the bare 'national' word item alongside phrase items; 'na' probe likewise; words without successors still suppressed; compareRankedMatches ordering unchanged (phrase first). Update acceptance.test.ts item 7 and chain.test.ts gotcha comment to the new invariant. Mock nothing — real store + pipeline per existing test/chain.test.ts harness.
4. OUTPUT: rankMatches behavior where successor-bearing bare words survive suppression, for consumption by P1.M4.T2.S2 (arming) and P1.M5.T1.S1 (chain post-restore probe).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the suppression-loop comment in query.ts and the spec-referencing comments in the tests. No config surface change.

subtasks.title: Arm the chain on phrase acceptance (last-word successor semantics)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md BUG-005. The arming intercept (src/pi/provider.ts ~L351-375, inside applyCompletion) arms only: CHAIN_KEY_PREFIX keys (chain successor accepted → arm next) and single-token keys (whole word → arm lowercase). Phrase keys (contain a space) hit the empty else — 'never arms' (explicitly listed in the PRD's BUG-005 location). liveKeyByValue maps display value → store key; phrase keys are single-space-joined lowercase. ChainMachine arm(word) offers store.topSuccessors(word). NOTE: the PRD recommendation mentions arming from 'the phrase's first word', but per §07 chain mechanics topSuccessors(armed.word) is the NEXT-word continuation — arming the LAST word is the semantically correct continuation (accepting 'national renewable energy' should offer successors of 'energy', e.g. 'laboratory'); first-word arming would re-offer already-typed words. This deliberate deviation is documented in architecture/system_context.md BUG-005.
2. INPUT: Successor-aware suppression from P1.M4.T2.S1 (the bare word now co-presents, making both arming routes reachable); serialized after P1.M4.T1.S1 because both edit src/pi/provider.ts (different functions, same file).
3. LOGIC: In the arming intercept, add a phrase branch (still gated by config.enablePhrases): when the accepted key contains a space, arm the chain at the phrase's LAST word — `const words = key.split(' '); chain.arm(words[words.length - 1])` — delegating verbatim to current.applyCompletion unchanged (existing arming contract). Tests: after a full NREL replay, accept the phrase item via applyCompletion (per test/chain.test.ts armViaTab pattern), then the next getSuggestions must offer topSuccessors of the last word as CHAIN_KEY_PREFIX items; accepting one re-arms per existing chain semantics; enablePhrases=false → nothing arms.
